sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the National Insurance Company Limited aggrieved by the compensation granted by the Tribunal to the injured in M.V.O.P.No.748/2007, dated 26.04.2010.

2. Heard Smt.I.Maamu Vani, learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Appellant-Insurance Company who submits that no proof was filed before the lower Court showing that the driver of the offending vehicle had a valid licence.

In fact, charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence under Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act for not possessing valid driving licence to drive the offending vehicle.
3. The only ground alleged by the counsel is regarding the driver not holding a valid licence.

4. If it is the case of the Insurance Company that the driver was not holding valid driving licence, the burden shifts on to the Insurance Company to prove that there was no valid driving licence held by the driver.

Only for the reason of charge sheet being filed under Section 181 of the Motor Vehicle Act, the Tribunal, this Court cannot conclude that the driver was not holding valid driving licence and compensation cannot be granted.
5. Charge sheet is filed by the Investigating Officer who is the collector of facts and evidence and placed before the Criminal Court.
Only on the basis of charges being framed and evidence adduced by either of the parties the Criminal Court would come to the conclusion regarding the allegations made in the charge sheet.
Per se the contents of the charge sheet cannot be accepted as truth to decide whether compensation can be granted in a case filed by the claimants in the Motor Vehicles Act.
6. The ground raised by the Insurance Company is unacceptable.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
K.SURENDER, J Date: 16.04.2024 tk THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE K.SURENDER MACMA.No.1497 OF 2010 Dt.16.04.2024 tk M/S National Insurance Company ... vs G. Ratnam And
